findings.what: "If that leaves a square equal to a number below zero, there is no answer" is an absolute claim that the Complex numbers course in this folder will overturn, and it drops the explain text's careful "on the number line"; say "no answer on the number line (no real answer); Complex numbers comes back to this".

The working goes from "x² − 4x = (x − 2)² − 4" straight to "so it is −(x − 2)² + 14" with the note "4 + 10 = 14". It skips the line −((x − 2)² − 4) + 10 = −(x − 2)² + 4 + 10, where the minus turns −4 into +4. That is the sign step the research flags for a minus in front (Brilliant, Edexcel), and the explain text shows it but the screen does not.

findings.where: Screens 11 and 12, check line at x = 0
findings.what: Both screens check at x = 0, but the practice notes rightly say x = 0 "cannot catch a wrong sign in the bracket" (−(x + 2)² + 14 also gives 10 at x = 0). Check at x = 1 instead: −1 + 14 = 13 = −1 + 4 + 10 on screen 11, and 32 − 13 = 19 = 2 + 12 + 5 on screen 12.

No puzzle asks Dan to complete a square with a minus in front of x², which screen 11 only shows, although the brief names the negative leading coefficient as a documented error. One mixed screen could ask for it, e.g. −x² + 6x − 4 = −(x − 3)² + 5, highest at (3, 5).

This is the first time Dan halves a negative b himself. The tiles cannot show it, and before this a negative half appears only in one working line on screen 11, so a one-line SHOW of "half of −10 is −5, so the bracket is x − 5" before the mixed screens would close the gap.

The lowest point (−3, −9) is marked at 0.75 s, before the strip is cut (1.3 s) and the corner appears (3.0 s), so the effect shows up before its cause. Let the dot arrive with the amber drop at 3.4 s.
The half strip can be dragged, but its grip is transparent and has no cue like the slider's arrows, so once the demonstration ends nothing shows that it can be moved.
"x + 3 is √7 or −√7, about 2.65 either way" can read as if both are +2.65. Say "about 2.65 or −2.65", since dropping the ± is the slip lesson 5 targets.
It repeats on all 13 screens and describes tiles, a curve "beside them" and dragging, none of which apply on the graph-only screens 8 to 13. At 360 px it also costs about six lines before every task.

The small graph is bare crossed axes with no ticks, curve or point (360 light and dark moved pictures), so it reads as an empty crosshair. Hide it until Check, or give it the plain-number line or y-crossing as the graph screens do.

The brief says the lesson will say plainly that no MCA or SQA HN line names completing the square, and why it is taught anyway (it makes the formula and the graph make sense). Neither the explain text nor the screens say so.
"That is the case with no number in front of x² of the general rule" is a tangled sentence; e.g. "This is MathWorld's general rule for the case where x² has no number in front."

The mirror image about x = −3 is stated and shown with one pair of points (x = −1 and −5 both give −3), but the reason, that points the same distance either side give the same square, appears only in the explain text. One clause on screen would complete the why.
